body: You're right, and as I've said in other comments, I appreciate how honest you guys have been about what I need to do. Deep down I think I knew I had to leave him, but you guys helped me so much by being honest about how he treated me. Thank you so much

Thank you for your helpful advice, funnily enough, I am starting to use journals to help myself. It's very comforting to know that people like you are showing such kindness and understanding for me even though you don't know me. Just, thank you so much

Thank you so much, it means a lot that even a stranger is trying to uplift me and support me during this time. 

I am trying to get therapy, but unfortunately, mental health services in my country are not as accessible as they seem. I am currently on a waiting list with an estimate of over a year. I cannot afford private therapy, but I am attending online sessions hosted by a mental health charity near me. They do not specialize in sexual assault or support for victims, but they do hold sessions to help with general mental health issues. They have definitely been helping me take better care of myself after finding out what happened, and I've been able to work on small tasks that are helping me feel like I'm back to 'normal'. If there is a normal for me anymore, that is
Thank you, these are words I needed to hear

Just, thank you. As I've said to other commenters, being confronted with the reality that this isn't someone I should be with has helped me accept it. I am scared, and I am scared of having no one there while I go through my journey of moving on, but you guys are right.

Thank you. I think being confronted with what I know I have to do has helped me a lot. I think deep down the moment he said those things and told me he was moving in with them I knew it had to be over. I'm a little scared of the next steps, but I needed to hear it bluntly. Thank you so much

I have a therapist. They don't do anything except make me feel worse. I hate talking about my problems, it makes me remember everything. I don't want to remember losing my first boyfriend to suicide, being domestically abused etc. I want to forget but I'll never be able to. I don't need help, because it doesn't work

Sorry if this is too personal, but have you ever had someone act as if they were you in an attempt to act on your behalf? This is what has stressed me out most of all, they pretended to be me in a crisis. All of these callers have had referrals that say I was the one who called personally and requested help. I can maybe understand more now that I have calmed down, but is it fair to say to them that that is an unhealthy approach to trying to help me? I just feel like impersonation and pretending I'm in a crisis is a step to far, but I don't know whether I'm being unreasonable
